title: Where the Sky Learns to Fold

features.name: convergence point
features.desc-on-touch: The sky folds here in quarters, each edge learning where the others point. You trace the crease with your fingertip and feel the cardinal winds becoming one.

features.name: fold ledger
features.desc-on-touch: A standing directory of crease patterns, each line a horizon that learned to bend toward home instead of away.

features.name: edgewise chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A house so folded it becomes a point, but warm light shows at every crease. Inside, the walls meet themselves continuously.

features.name: compass that taught itself inward
features.desc-on-touch: The needle no longer points outward; it trembles at the center, having learned that home was the direction all along.

features.name: reflected margin
features.desc-on-touch: The edge between sky and ground has forgotten which side it belongs to. It gleams like a doubled thread.

inscription: the sky learned to fold by watching how tired edges come home

file.name: Cartography_of_Convergence_1994.txt
file.note: A surveyor's notes on a place where all directions began asking the same question, filed as if the answer had already arrived
